correctness.rationale: The seven vertex-pair orbits reduce to six distinct objective values. For a full petal the (trace,u,v) data are (7/4,3,3); each damaged petal has a directly invertible 1x1 or 2x2 block. The Schur-complement trace identity produces explicit rational scores with positive Schur denominators. The four differences between nonhub classes and the distinct-center class are (3m+3)/8, (9m+11)/20, (3m+1)/16, (3m+1)/36, all >0 for integer m>=2; the hub-vs-center gap is (3m-7)/4, giving the asserted phase transition, while m=1 follows from its three types. A standalone exact-rational checker independently verified 2293 finite checks and was not used as a substitute for this all-m proof.

originality.rationale: Exact statement-level searches and the material of three closely relevant full-text primary sources do not establish the evaluated six-orbit classification or its exact two-to-three-petal transition. General all-graph inverse-trace/joint-centrality/resistance representations do not imply the ranked optimal configurations without additional graph-specific work. Publication priority is explicitly conditional on literature coverage; indexed searches are not uniqueness proofs.
residual_risks: A differently named diamond bouquet, fan-windmill, or more general one-point-sum exact leader-placement theorem may exist in literature not identified by the available searches.
General all-graph centrality formulas imply numerical computability, and the distinction from a previously explicit optimality theorem must be preserved.
The independent audit and definitive publication-priority assessment have not been performed.

value.rationale: For a natural infinite family made from identical short-path modules joined to a single hub, an exact two-control-input decision switches between three qualitatively different vertex-placement geometries as the module count changes. The complete optimizer set, exact objective, nonhub runner-up and strict gap quantify that decision, including a nonobvious equality between second-leader vertex degrees for all larger networks. This is an actual full-parameter classification rather than a small finite table or reformulated generic optimization criterion.
